bib.title: LLMS GET LOST IN MULTI-TURN CONVERSATION

read.skipped: References skimmed only. Table 1 and Figure 6 text is column-scrambled in the cache; read from the extracted number order.

question: How much does LLM performance drop when a task's requirements are revealed gradually over several conversation turns instead of in one fully specified instruction, and why?
hypothesis: Multi-turn, underspecified conversation degrades LLM performance relative to single-turn fully specified instructions, mainly through unreliability, because models make early assumptions and over-rely on their earlier answers.
contributions: Sharded simulation: a semi-automatic way to turn single-turn benchmark instructions into multi-turn underspecified ones
Large-scale simulation (200,000+ conversations, 15 LLMs, six tasks) showing an average 39% drop
Decomposition of the drop into small aptitude loss and large unreliability increase
Four behavioural causes: premature answers, answer bloat, loss-in-middle-turns, verbosity
Tests of agent-style remedies (RECAP, SNOWBALL) and lower temperature, neither of which closes the gap

method.summary: Single-turn instructions from six benchmarks are split into 'shards' (one fact each). An LLM-simulated user (GPT-4o-mini) reveals one shard per turn to the assistant under test, whose answer attempts are extracted and scored with the original benchmark metric. The same instructions are run FULL, CONCAT and SHARDED, ten times each, and scored by average performance, aptitude (90th percentile) and unreliability (90th minus 10th percentile).
method.task: multi-turn underspecified generation (code, SQL, API calls, math, table captioning, summarisation)

datasets.name: Code (HumanEval + LiveCodeBench v5 call-based, Easy/Medium)
datasets.size: 100 sharded instructions (45 from HumanEval's 164 problems, rest from LiveCodeBench)
datasets.preprocessing: sharded with the 4-step process; scored by test-case functional accuracy

datasets.name: Database (Spider 1.0 validation)
datasets.size: 107 sharded instructions (from 433 queries after dropping EASY)
datasets.preprocessing: schema in system message; execution match on multiple databases

datasets.name: Actions (BFCL V3 Parallel)
datasets.preprocessing: tool docs in system message; official BFCL semantic-equivalence checker

datasets.name: Math (GSM8K main)
datasets.preprocessing: shuffled, sharded incrementally; exact match after standardisation

datasets.name: Data-to-text (ToTTo test)
datasets.preprocessing: 5 shards: table, highlighted cells, page name, section name, 10 random example captions; BLEU

datasets.name: Summary (Summary of a Haystack, mini-Haystacks)
datasets.size: 92 sharded instructions, 20 documents each, 10 shards of 2 documents
datasets.preprocessing: summaries capped at 300 words, over-length summaries truncated; Joint Score (LLM judge)

datasets.name: Translation (WMT 2019 document-level, de-en)
datasets.size: 30 documents, first 10 sentences, 5 shards of 2 sentences
datasets.preprocessing: BLEU; seventh task used only in Section 7.3

models.name: GPT-4o-mini (user simulator, strategy classifier, answer extractor)

inference.decoding: sampling at default settings; no other decoding detail given
inference.temperature: 1.0 (main); 0.0, 0.5, 1.0 for assistant and user in the temperature experiment
inference.max_tokens: 1,000 per response; 10,000 for o3 and Deepseek-R1
inference.samples: N=10 simulations per (model, instruction, simulation type), 600 instructions x 3 types x 15 models = 200,000+ conversations; temperature experiment 20 runs per condition; gradual sharding 10 per instruction and model; RECAP/SNOWBALL N=10
inference.prompting: minimal system instruction with task context (schema, tool list, 'math problems'); assistant is not told the conversation is multi-turn or underspecified; user simulator is a lazy-user prompt revealing at most one shard per turn

parameters.shard_count_per_instruction: 3 or more (filter: fewer than 3 segments rejected)
parameters.sharding_acceptance_threshold: P_CONCAT >= 0.8 P_FULL and P_SHUFFLE-CONCAT >= 0.8 P_FULL, 10 runs each
parameters.recap_prompt:
Just to reiterate:
 - [past utterance 1]
- [past utterance 2]

 Also,
[current utterance]
parameters.conversation_end: correct answer attempt, or no unrevealed shards at start of a turn
parameters.strategy_classes: 7: answer attempt, clarification, interrogation, discussion, hedging, refusal, missing

other.manual_sharding_effort: 1-4 hours per task for 90-120 instructions; average 3 hours per 100 instructions; 1-3 minutes to inspect and edit one instruction
other.hardware: not stated; Llama-3.1-8B, OLMo2, Phi-4 run through local Ollama

metrics.name: Averaged performance P
metrics.definition: mean over N simulations of score S_i (0-100)

metrics.name: Aptitude A90
metrics.definition: 90th percentile of S over N simulations, per instruction, averaged over corpus

metrics.name: Unreliability U90_10
metrics.definition: 90th percentile minus 10th percentile of S per instruction, averaged over corpus; reliability R = 100 - U

metrics.name: Task scores
metrics.definition: binary correctness mapped to 0/100 for Code (tests), Database (execution match), Actions (BFCL checker), Math (exact match); BLEU for Data-to-text and Translation; Joint Score (coverage and citation, LLM judge) for Summary

eval.protocol: N=10 stochastic runs per cell, metrics per instruction then averaged; no significance tests or confidence intervals reported; simulator validity checked by manual annotation (Table 5).

prompts.purpose: User simulator (opening of prompt; full rules in Appendix O.2; sharding, classifier and extractor prompts in Appendix O)
prompts.text: You are simulating a user of an interactive LLM system (like ChatGPT). The user is inherently lazy, and answers in short form, providing only minimal information to the system. You should not be proactive.

evidence.quote: We set the maximum response length to 1,000 tokens for all models, and did not observe models exceeding this limit frequently when generating responses.

results.claim: Every model degrades on every task from FULL to SHARDED, averaging -39%.
results.setup: Main experiment: 600 sharded instructions over six tasks, 15 LLMs, FULL/CONCAT/SHARDED, N=10 simulations per model and type, T=1.0.
results.note: Elsewhere the paper prints -35% (Fig 1 caption) and a 90% to 65% (25-point) drop (Introduction); the three are not reconciled in the text.
results.quote: with an average degradation of -39%

results.claim: Single-turn average performance falls to 65% from 90%, a 25-point drop.
results.setup: Main experiment: 600 sharded instructions over six tasks, 15 LLMs, FULL/CONCAT/SHARDED, N=10 simulations per model and type, T=1.0. Averaged over models and tasks.
results.quote: a 25-point drop from single-turn performances of 90%

results.claim: CONCAT stays near FULL, so the SHARDED drop is not due to information lost in sharding.

limits: Fully automated, LLM-simulated user; authors say conversations are not representative of human-AI conversation and the degradation is likely an underestimate of real-world unreliability.
Shards are minimal and one is revealed per turn, which the authors admit can look adversarial; the final turn always completes the specification.
Analytical tasks only; creative or open-ended tasks untested.
English text only, no other languages or modalities.
Explanations of the drop (premature answers, bloat, verbosity, middle-turn loss) are correlational analyses of logs; the causal mechanisms are stated as hypotheses.
Remedies (RECAP, SNOWBALL, temperature) tested on only GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini; gradual sharding likewise two models.
No confidence intervals or significance tests; N=10 per cell.
Closed-API model versions (2024-2025 snapshots) have since been superseded, so the absolute numbers have dated.
Reasoning-model max tokens raised to 10,000; no study of larger thinking budgets.

terms.definition: a set of smaller instructions that jointly deliver the same information as the original instruction; shard 1 states the high-level intent
an estimate of a model's 90th percentile score on a given instruction, a best-case metric
the gap between the 90th and 10th percentile scores for an instruction
when LLMs take a wrong turn in multi-turn conversation, they get lost and do not recover
answer attempts grow longer across turns because the LLM keeps relying on its earlier assumptions
lost-in-the-middle occurring across conversation turns: first and last turns weigh more than middle ones
CONCAT lists all shards in one turn; RECAP adds a final turn restating all shards; SNOWBALL restates all revealed shards at every turn
